questoes.pergunta: At the fintech Lumen, senior developer Carla configured Claude Code to always use `FluentValidation` in DTOs, and it works well for her. A newly hired developer cloned the same repository, and Claude generates manual validation with `if` statements. Carla's instruction is in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. What is the most appropriate fix?
opcoes: Ask the new developer to copy Carla's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to their machine
Create a `PostToolUse` hook that rewrites manual validations to FluentValidation
Move the instruction to the project's `CLAUDE.md`, versioned in the repository
Put the instruction in the repository's `CLAUDE.local.md`
questoes.explicacao: The instruction is a team convention, but it was at the user level (personal). The right place is the project's CLAUDE.md, shared via git.
feedbacks: Solves it for one person, by hand, and breaks again with the next hire; the convention remains outside the repository.
A disproportionate solution: rewriting code via a hook is complex and fragile for something that is style guidance.
Correct: a team convention goes at the project level, versioned.
CLAUDE.local.md is personal and gitignored; the team still wouldn't receive it.

questoes.pergunta: Rafael works in the team's repository and wants Claude Code to use the URL of his personal sandbox environment (`https://rafael-sbx.internal`) and a test dataset that only he uses. His colleagues should not see this information. Where should he record it?
opcoes: In `CLAUDE.local.md` at the project root, kept out of git
In the project's `CLAUDE.md`, in a "Rafael's Preferences" section
In `.claude/settings.json`, under the `env` key
In a `CLAUDE.md` inside `src/`, which only loads on demand
questoes.explicacao: A personal preference specific to this project → CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored).
feedbacks: Correct: it is personal and restricted to this project.
Would version personal data for the whole team and pollute everyone's context.
`.claude/settings.json` is shared (versioned); it would still go to everyone.
A subdirectory CLAUDE.md is also versioned; loading on demand doesn't make it private.

questoes.pergunta: A logistics company has a .NET solution with 38 projects, and the tests live next to the code (`*Tests.cs`) in each project. The team wants the testing conventions (xUnit, AAA, no `Thread.Sleep`) to be applied whenever Claude touches tests, without weighing on the context when it is editing production code. What is the best configuration?
opcoes: A `CLAUDE.md` with the conventions in each of the 38 projects
A "Tests" section in the root `CLAUDE.md`
A `/test-conventions` skill that developers invoke when they remember to
A `.claude/rules/tests.md` file with `paths: ["**/*Tests.cs"]`
questoes.explicacao: A convention that cuts across directories → a rule with a `paths` glob: it loads only when touching matching files and covers future projects.
feedbacks: Duplication in 38 places, risk of divergence, and a new project starts without the rule.
Works, but it always loads, including when Claude is in production code: that is the context cost you wanted to avoid.
Depends on remembering to invoke it; a convention that must always apply is not a skill.
Correct: path-based scope, a single file, covers future folders.

questoes.pergunta: The root `CLAUDE.md` of a SaaS product has grown to 1,800 lines, mixing React, ASP.NET Core, and Terraform rules. The team reports that Claude frequently ignores rules and that sessions start with an already heavy context. What is the best action?
opcoes: Repeat the most important rules in CAPITAL LETTERS at the top of the file
Slim down the root CLAUDE.md and move each area's rules to rules with `paths` (or CLAUDE.md files in the corresponding subdirectories)
Split the file into three and import them with `@frontend.md`, `@backend.md`, and `@infra.md`
Configure `claudeMdExcludes` to exclude the root CLAUDE.md
questoes.explicacao: An overly large file dilutes attention and costs context. Instructions that apply only to part of the code should load on demand (rules with paths or a subdirectory CLAUDE.md).
feedbacks: Attacks the symptom; the file remains huge and the context remains heavy.
Correct: less content always loaded, and the specific content loaded when relevant.
Tempting, but imports load at startup along with CLAUDE.md: it organizes the text, it doesn't reduce the context.
Would exclude the team's general rules; claudeMdExcludes is for skipping other teams' CLAUDE.md files in a monorepo.

questoes.pergunta: A team wants a daily report of open issues, generated at 7 a.m. even with all laptops turned off, and also triggerable by a GitHub event. The data comes only from the public GitHub API. Which scheduling option matches these requirements?
opcoes: A scheduled task in a developer's desktop app
A `/loop` in a session left open on someone's laptop
A cloud routine
A `SessionStart` hook that generates the report when someone opens Claude Code
questoes.explicacao: It needs to run with the machines turned off and can be triggered by a GitHub event, so it's a cloud routine. A local task makes sense when you need access to files or a private network.
feedbacks: Runs on the developer's machine: if it's turned off, it doesn't run.
`/loop` lives inside an open session; it dies with it.
Correct.
Only runs when someone opens a session; it isn't scheduling.

questoes.pergunta: In a healthtech company's repository, the `.env` file contains production database credentials. CLAUDE.md already says "never read the .env", but in a debugging session Claude opened the file. What is the appropriate fix?
opcoes: Add `"deny": ["Read(./.env)"]` to `permissions` in the project's `.claude/settings.json`
Rewrite the CLAUDE.md instruction with more emphasis and an example
Move the instruction to a rule in `.claude/rules/` without `paths`
Ask developers to use plan mode in debugging sessions
questoes.explicacao: A critical security rule needs deterministic enforcement: a permission deny prevents the read, something CLAUDE.md (probabilistic) doesn't guarantee.
feedbacks: Correct: a deterministic block, versioned for the team.
It's still a prompt: it reduces the chance, it doesn't eliminate it. The anti-pattern of a critical rule only in the prompt.
A rule is also text in the context; same probabilistic nature as CLAUDE.md.
Plan mode allows reads; it doesn't prevent reading the .env.

questoes.pergunta: A .NET team wants, for all developers in the repository, `dotnet test` to run without a permission prompt and `git push --force` to always be blocked. Which configurations achieve this? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Write in CLAUDE.md: "feel free to run tests and never use push --force"
Add `"allow": ["Bash(dotnet test *)"]` to `.claude/settings.json`
Add both rules to the `.claude/settings.local.json` of whoever sets it up
Start all sessions with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`
Add `"deny": ["Bash(git push --force *)"]` to `.claude/settings.json`
questoes.explicacao: A prefix allow and a deny in the project's shared settings: deterministic and versioned for everyone.
feedbacks: Text doesn't grant permissions or block commands; it's probabilistic.
Correct: the prefix allows `dotnet test` with any arguments.
settings.local.json is personal and gitignored; the team doesn't receive it.
Turns off all checks: far beyond what was asked and unsafe on the developer's machine.
Correct: deny is evaluated first and no allow creates an exception.

questoes.pergunta: An insurance company's security team needs to ensure that no developer at the company uses `WebFetch` in Claude Code, in any repository, with no possibility of a project or user reverting this. Where should this be configured?
opcoes: In the `.claude/settings.json` of each company repository
In each developer's `~/.claude/settings.json`, via an onboarding script
In a managed CLAUDE.md with the instruction "don't use WebFetch"
In managed settings, with `permissions.deny` for `WebFetch`
questoes.explicacao: An organization policy that no one can override → managed settings (top of the precedence order), with a deny for the tool.
feedbacks: It has to be in every repo, and a new repository starts without it; plus, it doesn't cover use outside those repos.
The developer can edit their own file; it isn't enforced.
A managed CLAUDE.md is behavioral guidance; blocking a tool is the job of settings (deny).
Correct: managed overrides everything and deny is deterministic.

questoes.pergunta: At Planetário Software, the skill `.claude/skills/migration/SKILL.md` has `description: "Database utility"`. When developers ask "create a migration for the orders table", Claude writes the migration by hand instead of using the skill. Invoking `/migration` manually works. What is the simplest adjustment?
opcoes: Add `disable-model-invocation: true` to force its use
Rewrite the `description` saying what the skill does and when to use it (e.g., "Creates EF Core migrations... Use when asked for a migration, a schema change, or a new table")
Convert the skill into `.claude/commands/migration.md`
Add `context: fork` so the skill runs in a subagent
questoes.explicacao: The `description` is the auto-loading criterion. If it's too vague, Claude doesn't realize the skill applies.
feedbacks: Does the opposite: it prevents Claude from invoking it on its own.
Correct: the description is the trigger for the choice.
Commands and skills have been merged; changing the format doesn't improve the trigger (and loses skill features).
Changes where the skill runs, not whether it is chosen.

questoes.pergunta: A `/release` skill contains in its body: "In this run, update the version to 2.3.0 and generate the changelog." In the following session, for another release, the developer edited the file to 2.4.0 in the middle of the conversation, without re-invoking the skill, and Claude kept using 2.3.0. What is the diagnosis and the best fix?
opcoes: The skill body enters the conversation once and is not reread; the skill should have permanent instructions and receive the version as an argument (`$0`/`$ARGUMENTS`)
Claude Code caches the skill for 24 hours; just clear the cache
The skill needs `context: fork` to be reread every turn
The version should be in CLAUDE.md, which is reread every turn
questoes.explicacao: Once invoked, the skill stays in the conversation as text and the file is not reread. Permanent instructions + parameters passed as arguments avoid stale hardcoded values.
feedbacks: Correct.
There is no 24-hour cache; the reason is that the body enters once and stays.
`context: fork` isolates execution in a subagent; it doesn't reread per turn.
Would just move a hardcoded value somewhere else; the release's variable data should come in as an argument.

questoes.pergunta: The `/map-dependencies` skill reads dozens of files to build a dependency map between projects. After using it, the main session becomes slow and Claude starts forgetting decisions made earlier. What is the most direct adjustment?
opcoes: Add `user-invocable: false`
Split the skill into five smaller skills
Add `context: fork` (with `agent: Explore`) so the skill runs in an isolated subagent and returns only the map
Run `/compact` before each use of the skill
questoes.explicacao: A noisy task that only needs to return a result → run it in an isolated context. The noise stays in the subagent; the main session receives only the conclusion.
feedbacks: Only changes who can invoke it; the noise remains in the main context.
Still reads the same files in the main context, just in pieces.
Correct.
A stopgap: it compacts after the damage is done and loses details; it doesn't prevent the noise.

questoes.pergunta: A company maintains 12 repositories and wants to distribute the same set of review skills, a security subagent, and audit hooks to all of them, with version control and without copying files repository by repository. Which mechanism?
opcoes: Copy `.claude/skills` and `.claude/agents` into each repository via a script
Put everything in each developer's `~/.claude/`
A managed CLAUDE.md describing the skills
Package it as a plugin (skills + subagents + hooks) and install it in the repositories
questoes.explicacao: A plugin is the distributable package of skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP, with a namespace: built for sharing across repositories and teams.
feedbacks: Works, but it's the duplication you wanted to avoid; the copies diverge.
It stays personal and manual; there's no version control for the team.
Describing a skill in text neither creates nor distributes it.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Bruno uses Claude Code on his laptop and on his desktop. On the laptop, Claude already "knows" that the project uses `pnpm` (it learned this from an earlier correction); on the desktop, it insists on `npm`. No one wrote this in CLAUDE.md. What is the explanation and the fix?
opcoes: A sync bug; just log in again on the desktop
Auto memory is local to the machine; record the convention as an instruction in the project's CLAUDE.md (it belongs to the team) so it applies on any machine
The desktop uses a different Claude Code engine; you need to configure the extension
Auto memory only loads 200 lines; increase the limit in settings
questoes.explicacao: Auto memory (MEMORY.md) is written by Claude and stays on the machine; it isn't shared. Whatever needs to apply on every machine and for the team goes in the versioned CLAUDE.md.
feedbacks: It isn't a bug: auto memory doesn't sync across machines, by design.
Correct.
It's the same engine on all surfaces.
The limit isn't the problem: the memory simply doesn't exist on the other machine.

questoes.pergunta: On the payments team, the task is to "replace API key authentication with OAuth 2.0 in the three services, maintaining backward compatibility for a period". It hasn't been decided whether there will be a gateway or whether each service will validate tokens. How should the developer proceed in Claude Code?
opcoes: Use plan mode: explore the services, propose the approach, and only edit after the plan is approved
Ask for direct execution and review the diff at the end
Use `bypassPermissions` so the long task runs without interruptions
Open three direct sessions, one per service, in parallel
questoes.explicacao: A multi-service, architectural change with an undefined approach is the classic case for plan mode.
feedbacks: Correct.
Discovering the architectural decision in the middle of editing leads to costly rework.
Bypass doesn't resolve the uncertainty about the approach and is unsafe outside an isolated environment.
Parallelizes before deciding on the common architecture; the services may diverge.

questoes.pergunta: In which situations is plan mode the recommended choice? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Migrating from `Newtonsoft.Json` to `System.Text.Json` across more than 50 files, with custom converters
Fixing the `NullReferenceException` pointed to by the stack trace at line 88 of `OrderService.cs`
Changing the value of the `MaxRetries` constant from 3 to 5
A vague requirement: "improve the performance of the reports module", with no identified bottleneck
Adding a missing `using` that prevents compilation
questoes.explicacao: Plan mode is worthwhile for large/multi-file scope and for ambiguous requirements. Targeted, clear fixes go straight to execution.
feedbacks: Correct: multi-file, with decisions (converters) involved.
Targeted, with an exact location: direct execution.
Trivial: direct execution.
Correct: a confusing requirement calls for exploration and a proposal before editing.
Trivial and obvious: direct execution.

questoes.pergunta: The tech lead wants any developer in the repository to be able to delegate to a standardized "security reviewer" that analyzes controllers and authentication code and only reports findings, without modifying files. What is the most appropriate configuration?
opcoes: A section in CLAUDE.md: "when reviewing security, don't edit files"
Use the built-in general-purpose subagent with a detailed prompt each time
Create `.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md` with a clear `description` and `tools: Read, Grep, Glob`
Create the subagent in the tech lead's `~/.claude/agents/`
questoes.explicacao: A custom subagent at the project level (versioned), with restricted tools (least privilege) and a description that guides delegation.
feedbacks: Text doesn't restrict tools; the reviewer could still edit.
Works on a one-off basis, but it isn't standardized and general-purpose has access to all tools.
Correct.
It stays personal to the tech lead; the team doesn't receive it.

questoes.pergunta: A developer created `.claude/agents/docs-generator.md` with `permissionMode: bypassPermissions`, expecting the subagent to write documentation files without prompts. The main session runs in `default` and the prompts keep appearing. Why?
opcoes: The correct field is `permission-mode`, with a hyphen
Subagents can never write files
Claude Code must be restarted for the frontmatter to take effect
A subagent cannot escalate beyond the main conversation's mode; the right way is to allow the writes with `allow` rules (or use `acceptEdits` in the session)
questoes.explicacao: The parent's permissions flow down: a subagent configured with bypass doesn't get bypass in a default session. Allow what's needed with specific allow rules.
feedbacks: The field name is `permissionMode`; the problem isn't syntax.
Subagents such as general-purpose, or custom ones with Write, can write; it's Explore/Plan that are read-only.
Restarting doesn't change the rule against privilege escalation.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: In a 2,000-file repository, a developer asks Claude Code: "how does the payment refund flow work?" Which exploration approach follows recommended practice?
opcoes: Read all the `.cs` files first to have the complete context
Grep for entry points (e.g., `Refund`, the controller route), read what matters, and follow the dependencies with new Greps; or delegate the exploration to the Explore subagent
Glob for `**/*.cs` and read the first 50 results
Ask the developer to paste the relevant files into the conversation
questoes.explicacao: Incremental exploration: Grep → Read → Grep → Read. For a large volume, Explore returns only the conclusion.
feedbacks: A classic anti-pattern: reading everything up front uses up the window and degrades quality.
Correct.
Glob doesn't look at content; the first 50 by name may have nothing to do with refunds.
Shifts to the human work that the built-in tools do better.

questoes.pergunta: Claude attempted an `Edit` on `appsettings.json` replacing `"Enabled": false` with `"Enabled": true`, but the call failed: the snippet appears in four different sections. Only the `Cache` section should change. Which actions are appropriate? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Repeat the same Edit call
Use `replace_all: true` with the same snippet
Expand the `old_string` to include the `"Cache": {` line and its neighbors until the snippet is unique
Use Glob to locate the correct section
Read the file and rewrite it with Write, if that's safer than building a unique snippet
questoes.explicacao: Edit requires a unique snippet. Expand the snippet's context, or read and rewrite. `replace_all` would change all four sections, which is not what's wanted.
feedbacks: The same input fails the same way.
Would replace all four occurrences, but only the Cache one should change.
Correct.
Glob finds files by name; it doesn't locate snippets inside a file.
Correct: a valid alternative when building a unique snippet is complicated.

questoes.pergunta: At a consulting firm, half the team uses Claude Code in VS Code, some in JetBrains, and some in the terminal. The lead wants everyone to have the same conventions, the same skills, and the same permissions. What is the approach?
opcoes: Version CLAUDE.md, `.claude/skills/`, and `.claude/settings.json` in the repository: it's the same engine on all surfaces
Configure each IDE extension separately, since each one has its own engine
Standardize everyone on the terminal, because the extensions don't read CLAUDE.md
Keep one CLAUDE.md per surface (`CLAUDE.vscode.md`, `CLAUDE.jetbrains.md`)
questoes.explicacao: The CLI, IDEs, desktop, and web use the same engine and read the same configuration files.
feedbacks: Correct.
False premise: it's the same engine.
The extensions read CLAUDE.md, skills, and settings normally.
Those files don't exist as a convention; it would duplicate content unnecessarily.
